segments.text: Notebooks made exploring data fast. But they were built for one person, typing into cells.
Exuvia is the notebook for the AI era: a workbench where you and your agent build side by side.
Every step is a plain Python or SQL file. Its inputs are just function parameters and table names, so the steps wire themselves into a graph.
Edit a node, run it, and see the data. Only what's stale runs again, and every output is kept: cached, and content-addressed.
Unlike a notebook, any step can run on its own schedule. When its output changes, everything downstream follows.
And you're not working alone. An AI agent reads, writes, runs and debugs nodes, right on the canvas, with the same tools you have.
Use the built-in agent, or bring Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, over MCP.
And the graph is not the end product. Views turn outputs into custom interfaces: React files that only read, with no back end to write.

And there is no git required. Exuvia takes a different approach to version control: every save is kept, yours or the agent's, with nothing to stage, commit or push. Every output remembers the exact code that made it, so your agent spends its time on the analysis, not on commits and branches.
Start on your laptop with one command. Move to a hub when the team shows up.
Exuvia. Notebooks, for the AI era.
